concepts.def: Slow CO2 removal as rain breaks down silicate rocks.
Ocean process moving carbon to deep waters via shells.
Carbon Capture and Storage at industrial sources.
Direct Air Capture pulling CO2 from ambient air.
Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage.
Frozen soil carbon at risk as Arctic warms.

walkthroughs.body_html: The slow carbon cycle moves around 0.2 GtC per year. Rainwater becomes weakly acidic with CO2, weathering silicate rocks. Calcium and bicarbonate ions wash to the sea, where marine organisms make CaCO3 shells. When they die, shells form limestone, locking carbon away for millions of years until volcanic activity returns it as CO2.

CCS captures CO2 from flue gases at power plants or factories and injects it underground in deep saline formations or depleted oil fields. DAC removes CO2 from ambient air at higher cost (currently 100 to 600 dollars per tonne). BECCS grows biomass which absorbs CO2, burns it for energy and captures the emissions, giving net-negative outcomes if done right.

Arctic permafrost holds around 1500 GtC of frozen organic carbon, almost twice the atmospheric stock. As temperatures rise, microbes wake and decompose this material, releasing CO2 and methane. This positive feedback could add 100 to 200 GtC by 2100 under high-emissions scenarios, accelerating warming further.
